messages:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding quantized v2 of bert-qa shows a weird holdout regression on the eval dashboard, not a perf/latency issue but quality drift. https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/models/bert-qa-v2

sam: saw that — which metric?

maya: exact_match dropped from 82.1% -> 75.3% on the standard promptset. AUC-ish reranker score also shifted. Screenshot attached in the dashboard.

eva: CI for the eval-runner also reported a flaky shard run earlier today, Jenkins job #4246 failed with shard mismatch. Could be leakage or shard ordering.

liam: @eva can you paste the runner log snippet? I want to check the shuffle/seed behavior.

ci-bot: [ci] build 4246: eval-runner: failed on tests/eval/fixtures_leakage.py::test_holdout_consistency (exit code 1)

eva: here —
```
2026-03-19T22:12:03Z runner: shard loader checksum mismatch: expected 0x1a2b3c4d got 0x9f8e7d6c
2026-03-19T22:12:03Z runner: seed=42, rng_state=0x7f3a9
2026-03-19T22:12:03Z fixture-manager: TTL expired for synthetic cassette 2026-03-18T03:00:00Z
```

maya: TTL expired for synthetic cassette — hmm. We regenerated synthetic fixtures for the quant run last night; maybe some fixtures got re-used across holdout.

sam: Could be a synthetic generation non-determinism: last deploy changed the tokenization pipeline. Did the promptset fingerprint change?

liam: quick checks:
```
# list promptset fingerprints
python -m eval_tools.promptset --list-fingerprints --path=gs://redwood-evals/promptsets/bert-qa
# check shard checksums
sha256sum /mnt/eval/shards/bert-qa-*.idx
```

tony: also check CI sharders: we recently merged a small change to RunnerShardIterator that changed slice boundaries when total_examples % shards != 0. Could cause sample bleeding between CI golden run and local regen.

maya: reran the golden-run locally with pinned seed and old tokenizers from the release tag; exact_match stayed at 82.0 — so the model itself is fine. The regression only appears when using the new quantized runtime + freshly generated synthetic fixtures.

sam: that points to fixture leakage or prompt canonicalization change. Two hypotheses: (1) synthetic generator nondet (timestamp or RNG leak into artifact name), (2) prompt normalization changed causing different match scoring.

liam: I pushed a small debug patch to the eval-runner to log prompt IDs and prompt fingerprints at ingestion time. If you can re-run the failing job with `EVAL_DEBUG=1` we get the diff.

maya: launching job 4247 with EVAL_DEBUG=1 now. Command:
```
./deploy/eval-runner --model bert-qa-v2-quant --promptset gs://redwood-evals/promptsets/bert-qa:v3 --fixtures /mnt/fixtures/quant-v2 --env EVAL_DEBUG=1
```

ci-bot: [ci] job 4247 queued by maya

eva: note — dashboard metric definitions: exact_match is computed with post-normalization step. If tokenization changed that normalization may cause big gaps. Check `eval/metrics/normalizers.py` diff in last three commits.

sam: I looked — a small change to whitespace normalization was merged two days ago in PR #889. It strips leading/trailing newlines earlier in the pipeline. Could affect exact_match on QA prompts where gold answers include trailing line markers.

tony: also found one place where synthetic fixture filenames include a timestamp suffix when TTLs are set, which makes cache keys differ between runs. That could lead to older fixtures being expired and new variants inserted into holdout. PR coming.

maya: job 4247 logs are up: initial pass shows 12 out of 120 prompt IDs in holdout are mapping to fixtures with different fingerprint than the golden-run. Dumps attached in logs.

liam: good catch. If it's only 10% of holdout changing, that can easily explain a 6–7% EM drop. Let's revert normalization change in a branch and re-run synthetic generator with deterministic seed and stricter artifact naming.

sam: for CI: add a gate that compares promptset fingerprint between golden-run and new-run and fails early with a clear message if they differ. We can add a small check in the eval workflow YAML.

maya: agreed. Also config suggestion: pin synthetic TTL for release-quality runs so we don't accidentally regen during an onboarding window.

eva: I'll open two PRs: one to pin TTLs in generator config, another to add promptset fingerprint check in CI.

liam: I'll prepare rollback for whitespace normalizer and a test that asserts fingerprint stability across tokenizer versions.

tony: and I'll fix the fixture filename timestamping bug.

maya: thanks everyone. If CI 4247 still shows mismatches after the fixes we'll triage deeper (kv-cache, prefix caching in quant runtime). For now, action items: eva (PRs), sam (CI gate), liam (rollback branch + test), tony (filename fix).

ci-bot: [ci] job 4247: started on runner-11

maya: ping @sam when job finishes, will verify dashboard numbers and close the onboarding ticket if green. :thumbsup:
